questions.text: Write short notes on: (a) JavaScript Callbacks and Promises, (b) DevOps culture and Containerization (Docker), (c) Input sanitization and Content Security Policy (CSP).

Explain asynchronous JavaScript programming. Compare Callbacks, Promises, and async/await syntax. How does the JavaScript Event Loop (Call Stack, Web APIs, Task Queue, Microtask Queue) handle asynchronous operations without blocking the single thread?
questions.solutionOutline: JavaScript runs on single thread with run-to-completion semantics. Synchronous code executes on Call Stack. Asynchronous tasks (timers, fetch) are delegated to browser Web APIs. Upon completion, callback enters Task/Callback Queue (macrotask) or Microtask Queue (Promises, queueMicrotask). Event loop prioritizes drain of Microtask queue before picking next macrotask.

questions.text: Explain the React Component Lifecycle and React Hooks. Differentiate between useState, useEffect, useContext, and useMemo with functional component code snippets.
questions.solutionOutline: React hooks allow functional components to use state and lifecycle features. useState manages local reactive state. useEffect runs side effects (API calls, subscriptions) with optional dependency array and cleanup function. useContext accesses React Context without prop drilling. useMemo memoizes computed values across re-renders to prevent expensive recalculations.

questions.text: Design a RESTful API for an Online E-Commerce System with endpoints for user authentication, product catalog, cart management, and order checkout. Explain HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH) and standard HTTP status codes (200, 201, 400, 401, 403, 404, 500).
questions.solutionOutline: REST principles: stateless, uniform interface, resource-oriented URIs (/api/v1/products, /api/v1/cart, /api/v1/orders). POST creates resources (201 Created), GET retrieves (200 OK), PUT replaces, PATCH partially updates, DELETE removes (204 No Content). Status codes: 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found, 500 Internal Server Error.

questions.text: Explain Web Security vulnerabilities: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS: Stored, Reflected, DOM-based), Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF), and SQL Injection. Describe comprehensive mitigation strategies for each.
questions.solutionOutline: XSS injects malicious client-side JavaScript (mitigated by context-aware output encoding, Content Security Policy, and HttpOnly cookie flags). CSRF tricks victim browser into executing unwanted actions (mitigated by Anti-CSRF tokens and SameSite=Lax/Strict cookie attributes). SQL injection injects malicious SQL statements into database queries (mitigated by Prepared Statements / Parameterized Queries and ORM frameworks).

questions.text: Compare Session-based Authentication with Token-based Authentication (JSON Web Tokens - JWT). Explain the three parts of a JWT (Header, Payload, Signature) and secure cookie storage flags (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite).
questions.solutionOutline: Session-based: server maintains state in memory/database, client stores session ID in cookie; stateful, harder to scale across distributed servers. JWT: stateless cryptographic token. Parts: Header (algorithm & token type), Payload (claims like user id, exp), Signature (HMACSHA256(base64(header) + '.' + base64(payload), secret)). Cookies: HttpOnly blocks JS document.cookie access (anti-XSS), Secure requires HTTPS, SameSite protects against CSRF.

questions.text: Explain the Model-View-Controller (MVC) architectural pattern in server-side web development (e.g., Express.js / Node.js or Django). Explain middleware functions, routing, and database ORM/ODM integration.
questions.solutionOutline: MVC separates concern: Model represents data schema and business rules (e.g. Mongoose, Prisma, SQLAlchemy); View renders user presentation; Controller receives requests, interacts with Model, and serves View or JSON response. Middleware functions access req, res, and next() for logging, body parsing, CORS, and authentication verification before route handlers.

questions.text: Explain CSS Grid Layout versus CSS Flexbox. Write CSS rules for responsive design using Media Queries to adjust a three-column card layout into a single-column stacked layout on mobile viewports.
questions.solutionOutline: Flexbox is one-dimensional (row OR column), ideal for component layouts and alignment. CSS Grid is two-dimensional (rows AND columns simultaneously), ideal for overall page structure. Media queries use @media (max-width: 768px) to redefine grid-template-columns from repeat(3, 1fr) to 1fr for responsive mobile displays.

questions.chapter: Web Application Deployment and Modern Trends
questions.text: What is a Progressive Web App (PWA)? Explain Service Workers, Web App Manifest (manifest.json), Cache Storage API, and offline capabilities with application lifecycle.
questions.solutionOutline: PWAs deliver app-like experiences within web browsers. Key pillars: 1) Web App Manifest (provides name, icons, theme-color, standalone display); 2) Service Worker (background client proxy script intercepting network fetch events); 3) HTTPS requirement; 4) Cache Storage API implementing cache-first or stale-while-revalidate strategies enabling complete offline accessibility.

questions.text: Explain WebSockets and Server-Sent Events (SSE). Contrast full-duplex WebSocket communication with traditional HTTP long-polling for real-time collaborative applications.
questions.solutionOutline: HTTP long-polling repeatedly opens new HTTP connections with large header overhead. WebSocket establishes persistent, full-duplex, bi-directional TCP connection initiated via HTTP Upgrade handshake (ws:// or wss://), sending lightweight binary/text frames with minimal 2-byte header overhead. SSE provides unidirectional server-to-client streaming over standard HTTP text/event-stream.

questions.text: Explain the Virtual DOM mechanism in React. How does React's Reconciliation and Diffing algorithm update the browser DOM efficiently?
questions.solutionOutline: Virtual DOM is a lightweight in-memory JavaScript representation of real DOM. Direct DOM manipulation is slow due to browser layout and repaint cycles. When state changes, React renders new Virtual DOM tree, computes diff with previous tree using O(n) heuristic reconciliation rules (different element types produce different trees, keys identify list elements across renders), and batches minimal updates to real DOM.

questions.text: Compare GraphQL with RESTful API architecture. Explain how GraphQL resolves over-fetching and under-fetching problems using Queries, Mutations, and Subscriptions.
questions.solutionOutline: REST uses fixed endpoints returning predefined data structures; fetching related data often requires multiple roundtrips (under-fetching) or returns excess fields (over-fetching). GraphQL uses single endpoint (/graphql) with strongly typed schema. Clients query exactly the fields they need. Queries fetch data, Mutations modify data, Subscriptions push real-time updates over WebSockets.

questions.text: Explain Single Page Application (SPA) vs Multi-Page Application (MPA), and Client-Side Rendering (CSR) vs Server-Side Rendering (SSR) vs Static Site Generation (SSG) in modern web development frameworks.
questions.solutionOutline: SPA loads single HTML shell and dynamic JS bundles; routing handled on client without page reloads. CSR renders HTML in browser JS (faster interactions, poor initial load & SEO). SSR generates full HTML per request on server (great SEO, fast FCP, heavier server load). SSG pre-renders static HTML at build time (fastest CDN delivery, ideal for blogs/docs).

questions.chapter: Web Application Deployment and Modern Trends
questions.text: Explain Web Performance Optimization techniques: Lazy Loading of images and components, Code Splitting, Asset Minification, CDN edge caching, and Core Web Vitals (LCP, FID/INP, CLS).
questions.solutionOutline: Performance optimization speeds loading and user responsiveness. Lazy loading defers off-screen images/routes using dynamic import() and IntersectionObserver. Code splitting breaks JS bundle into smaller chunks. Minification strips whitespace and comments. Core Web Vitals: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP < 2.5s), Interaction to Next Paint (INP < 200ms), Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS < 0.1).

questions.text: What is Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)? Explain Simple Requests vs Preflight Requests (OPTIONS method), Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers, and Content Security Policy (CSP).
questions.solutionOutline: Browser Same-Origin Policy (SOP) blocks web apps from requesting resources from different origin (domain, protocol, port). CORS relaxes this via HTTP response headers: Access-Control-Allow-Origin, Access-Control-Allow-Methods, Access-Control-Allow-Headers. Non-simple requests (custom headers, PUT/DELETE, application/json) trigger preflight HTTP OPTIONS request before actual request. CSP defines approved script/resource origins to prevent XSS.
